newsitem.title: UK: London clean tankers dull except for Med/East trade.
newsitem.headline: London clean tankers dull except for Med/East trade.

text.p: Clean tanker fixtures from the Mediterranean were particularly active for Far Eastern destinations although the rest of the market remained in the doldrums this week, shipping brokers said.
Rates generally fell and even the active Middle East-India route failed to fetch more than W175 for a 43,000 tonner, down from last week's W180.

"There was continuing interest in the Mediterranean for shipping product to the East, but on the Continent and in the Caribbeans a notable lack of enthusiasm and interest from charterers was discernible," brokers E.A. Gibson said in a report.
"Similarly, the Eastern markets proved lifeless and, as a consequence, owners struggled to maintain the previous week's rate levels," the report added.

A lack of available tonnage in the Med, particularly for spot, enabled some owners to improve their earnings, Gibson said. Typical gas oil liftings of 30,000 tonnes in the cross-Med paid around W180, virtually unchanged from last week. Naphtha cargoes of 27,500 tonnes achieved W207.5, up from last week's W205.

Caribbean business was dull although rates did pick up at the end of the week with the 28,500 tonne Ulyanovsk travelling the Caribs/US Atlantic Coast route fetching W265 and Conoco paying W267.5 for the Pbulk Runner.
"Unfortunately, with an increasing amount of available tonnage, it is unlikely that there will be any change in this situation prior to the May Day holiday," Gibson said.

The Inter-U.K./Cont market saw a limited amount of enquiry and fixing. Enquiry for longer-haul movements of gas oil to the East and of gasoline to the United States did not result in any fixtures, Gibson said.
They said a parcel of 35,000 tonnes has been on and off subjects throughout the week at around W200 for a Cont/USAC voyage.
